newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi army admits killing 126 returning refugees.
newsitem.headline: Burundi army admits killing 126 returning refugees.

text.p: Soldiers from Burundi's Tutsi-dominated army shot dead 126 Burundian Hutu refugees who had been expelled from Tanzania and tried to escape from a detention centre in Burundi, an army spokesman said on Saturday.
Lieutenant-Colonel Isaie Nibizi told Reuters the 126 refugees were killed late on Friday. "They were all shot and killed after they tried to escape from the centre," he said.
Nibizi condemned the killing, which took place in the northeast province of Muyinga, and said seven soldiers involved in the shooting had been arrested.
"The seven soldiers involved in the shootings have all been arrested and will be charged before courts of law," Nibizi said in a rare admission of wrongdoing by the army.

Jean-Luc Ndizeye, a spokesman for military leader Major Pierre Buyoya, told Reuters the government was investigating the incident. "We are aware of the incident and we're conducting our own investigations. We shall release more details as we progress with the investigations," Ndizeye said.

The latest killings in the war-torn and ethnically divided central African nation came a day after witnesses and other sources accused the army of massacring at least 83 civilians in a single operation last Sunday night near Rutegama in Muramvya province, about 65 km (40 miles) from the capital Bujumbura.

Burundi is at war between the army and Hutu rebels fighting for a greater political stake in the small tea and coffee- growing country whose military government and army are dominated by the Tutsi minority.
Burundi has remained unstable since the 1993 murder of the country's first freely elected president, Melchior Ndadaye, a Hutu. The civil war has cost at least 150,000 lives.

The head of the U.N. refugee agency in Burundi, Hitoshi Mise, told Reuters earlier that some 120 Burundian Hutu refugees accused of fomenting trouble in camps in Tanzania were expelled back to Burundi on Saturday. But Nibizi said the expulsions took place on Friday.
Mise declined to comment on the killings when later contacted by Reuters.

He said the expelled refugees were from Tanzania's Kitale camp which has been hit by factional fighting between Hutu groups since December. U.N. officials say more than 10 refugees had died in clashes.

Mise said the fighting pitted members of Palepehutu, a radical group of Hutus opposed to Burundi's Tutsi junta, against elements of the National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD), a guerrilla group also opposed to the junta.
Mise said all the expelled were members of the Palepehutu.

Tanzania is home to over 80,000 Burundian Hutu refugees who have fled war. Last month the east African nation, a traditional haven for refugees in the strife-torn region, ordered more than 500,000 Rwandan refugees back home.
Burundi's 25,000-strong army has been accused by human rights organisations of committing massacres against the majority Hutus.

Some of the recent victims are former refugees, forced from their camps in neighbouring eastern Zaire late last year because of a rebellion there. They returned to Burundi reluctantly and hundreds have been killed, relief workers say.
Buyoya was installed by the army last July after a coup against the previous coalition government.
